name: Old English vinyl combination briefcases
flaw: Combination locks have the codes sealed inside the cases — only a safe-cracker can open them. Also rejects, also nicked.

name: Boxes of lead
supplier: Bought hidden under a load of bricks
flaw: Originally meant for a DIY nuclear fallout shelter. Heavy, suspicious, hard to shift.

name: Porcelain statuette of Kubera
flaw: Vimmal and Mr Ram are working together. The 'priceless' statue is worth £17 on Portobello Road.

name: 'Yves Saint Dior' Parfum de Toilette
flaw: A bath tub of vile yellow liquid decanted into branded bottles in the lounge, with Grandad stamping the boxes.

name: 'Awayday Gold' yellow paint
flaw: Nicked from a storage shed at Clapham Junction. Used for railway tunnel signs because it's luminous — glows in the dark.

name: Deep-sea diver's watches
flaw: Tells the time in every capital city in the world — except London.

name: Broken lawnmower engines
flaw: Rusted and broken — Del bought them drunk down the One-Eleven Club. Scrap value about £20.

name: Battery-powered toy yap-yap dogs
flaw: Cheap, naff, and you have to leg it the moment you see Old Bill.

name: Smoke-damaged industrial fire alarms
flaw: Industrial models, all 'guaranteed — sort of — to be in perfect working order'.

name: Fresh-caught salmon
flaw: Poached from a private estate, with bribes to a corrupt gamekeeper. Plus an axe murderer's loose in the area.

name: Sun tan lotion
flaw: Flogged in cold weather. Del eventually has to 'knock some out' to cover Albert's stunt-man losses.

name: Kandy Dolls
flaw: Each doll has a different voice chip meant for another toy entirely.
episode: S4E4 It's Only Rock and Roll

name: Booking for 'A Bunch of Wallies' (Rodney's band)
flaw: Sold to the Shamrock Club as a real act. They are appalling. The gig ends in a brawl.
target: Liam at the Shamrock Club, Deptford
episode: S4E4 It's Only Rock and Roll

name: A baby (Anna's unborn child)
flaw: Sold as 'a boy' to Boycie & Marlene. Turns out to be a mixed-race girl. Anna decides to keep her anyway.

name: Nomad cordless mobile telephones
flaw: Crackle, drop calls, generally useless. Del's still trying to flog them in the Nag's Head.

name: Ultraviolet home solarium / sunbed
flaw: Retails at £375 'normally'. Comes with a free plug-in telephone (and an extension) if you'll just take it.

name: Rajah 2000 home computers
flaw: BBC Masters in third-party Viglen cases with a stick-on badge. Flogged one to a vicar.

name: Lusty Linda & Erotic Estelle inflatable dolls
flaw: Filled with explosive propane gas due to a factory mix-up. Self-inflate. Will detonate if heated.

name: Video recorders
flaw: Continental current only. Won't run on British power without a transformer the size of a suitcase.

name: 'Fresh Jersey' tomatoes
flaw: Definitely not from Jersey. Trigger says they taste off.

name: 250 18-carat gold chains
flaw: Arnie fakes a heart attack mid-deal and escapes in a fake ambulance with his sons Gary and Steven.

name: Crimplene summer dresses with big flowers
flaw: Flogged at the market through a February of frost and sleet. Three months of unpaid rent.

name: Albanian car radios
flaw: Catch fire. One fitted in the Jolly Boys' coach blew up near Margate.

name: Romanian Riesling
flaw: Dodgy enough that Del had to lay low and skip the country.

name: Peckham Spring mineral water
flaw: It's tap water. Bottling plant is the lounge. Drained the local reservoir; possibly contaminated by a yellow liquid Del, Trigger and Denzil dumped earlier.

name: Box of men's wigs
flaw: Del thought he was buying ladies' wigs to flog to old dears in the Nag's Head. They are very much not.
target: Old ladies in the Nag's Head

name: Clip-on ponytails
flaw: Aimed at the trendy market. Rodney unwillingly becomes the model.

name: Faulty paint sold to Dr Singh
flaw: Whatever was wrong with it, the doctor was still furious about it years later when Del came in for a vasectomy.

name: One-legged turkeys
flaw: Sold from the back of the Reliant. Tin says it all.
episode: Pre-series legend / referenced in Big Brother

name: DIY North Sea gas conversion kits
flaw: Sent Rodney (with chickenpox) to flog them on the Mountbatten Estate. Which is all-electric.

name: China cats playing 'How Much Is That Doggy in the Window'
flaw: A balls-up at the factory put the wrong chimes in. Cats playing a song about a dog.

name: 'Made in Britain' singing dolls
flaw: Sing a full repertoire of Chinese lullabies.

name: Digital watches
flaw: Play 36 different national anthems on the hour. Loudly.

name: Portable CD players
flaw: Fling the discs out like clay pigeons.

name: Hairdryers
flaw: Are actually paint strippers.

name: Infra-red 'miracle-cure' body massagers
flaw: Del and Albert hit the health market. They do not cure anything.

name: Mobile phones
flaw: Bring trouble with the Driscoll Brothers in the next episode.

name: Clapped-out motor
flaw: Brakes don't work. Rodney almost crashed it on the test drive.
